description:
The UN slavery vote just exposed the biggest lie about African history, reparations, and who really controlled the transatlantic slave trade. In March 2026, 123 countries voted yes. The US said no. All 27 EU nations abstained.
Here is what they are not telling you.
For over 150 years, one sentence has been used to block every serious reparations conversation — "Africans sold their own people." In this video, we trace exactly where that narrative came from, who built it, why the kingdoms that resisted the slave trade were erased from history, and what the UN vote actually means for Africa's future.

TO JOIN OUR MEMBERSHIP CLICK THE LINK
https://www.patreon.com/AfricaTodayClub763

We cover the Kingdom of Benin, which banned the slave trade and was destroyed for it in 1897. Queen Njinga of Angola, who fought Portuguese slavers for 30 years. The Moroccan invasion of the Songhai Empire and what it actually tells us about the trans-Saharan slave trade. The broken promise of 40 acres and a mule after the American Civil War. And the straight line between the financial architecture of the slave trade and what the IMF and World Bank are doing to African economies today.
The lie was never about history. It was always about who pays.
🔔 Subscribe for weekly deep dives into African geopolitics, power, and strategy.
👥 Join our Patreon for full source documents, extended research, and member discussions.
#AfricanHistory #Reparations #UNVote #TransatlanticSlaveTrade #africangeopolitics

comments.text:
Africa did fight back.
Not in whispers—but in war cries pressed into the soil,
in blood that knew the land by name.
They fought on African ground,
on the bones of ancestors who refused to be forgotten.

And still—
In the end, we were all bound.

Not always in chains that clanked and showed themselves,
but in something quieter, deeper—
to be made a slave in your own homeland,
to stand where you belong
and still have nowhere to run,
no distant shore to dream of—
because you are already home.

They did not need ships to conquer us here.
We were already fighting—
the same battles,
but rooted in the very earth that raised us.
Tell me, how do the enslaved send ships across oceans
When their war is beneath their own feet?

They stripped us—
not just of land,
but of name, of memory, of self.

They took the children,
placed them in quiet rows of obedience,
in schools that polished away identity
until only compliance remained.
They rewrote the past,
fed them stories carved to fit a conqueror’s truth,
and buried the rest beneath silence.

Centuries passed before we could begin to rise,
and even then—
Something had already been taken.

Because by the time freedom came,
The chains had changed form.
No iron. No shackles.

Just minds reshaped,
histories erased,
and a freedom that still had to be learned.
